claim: Smart roads and automation eliminate most human driving
originalWording: Smart roads and automation eliminate most human driving

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Automation removes more than half of human driving, retaining the forecast’s “most” threshold.
strict.rationale: 2019 road transport still relied predominantly on human drivers. Public driverless services are a real advance, but do not establish that most driving has been eliminated across the road system.

evidence.title: Automated Vehicle Safety — NHTSA
evidence.note: Live guidance checked for this review. Describes limited operating areas for automated fleets and driver-attention requirements of consumer vehicles; not a historical 2009 market census.

evidence.title: Waymo opens its fully driverless service to the public
evidence.note: Geofenced Phoenix service, not all roads, universal ownership, or road-embedded guidance infrastructure.

evidence.title: WHO: Global road safety progress remains insufficient
evidence.note: 2021 global annual road deaths 1.19 million; about 5% below 2010. These are observed-year figures, not invented 2026 counts.

broader.criterion: Fully driverless commercial travel operates on public roads as a meaningful step toward reducing human driving.
broader.rationale: Waymo opened fully driverless public rides in Phoenix in 2020 and later expanded to additional metros, proving commercial driverless capability. Even charitably, however, geofenced robotaxis account for a minuscule share of total driving and do not fulfill eliminating most human driving.
changedConditions: Credits geofenced commercial robotaxis as partial without equating them to eliminating most driving
